title: Memoisation optimisation and the categorical-mass reading of the reducer
html:
Remark. Memoisation optimisation and the categorical-mass reading of the reducer

Optimisation: memoisation on basis elements

Each S_n has n! basis elements. We memoise the recursive tr_M on (w, n) via functools.lru_cache. For repeated atom evaluations within a single Python process (e.g., in the multi-atom witness pipeline), we compute basis-element traces once and re-use them. This yields an asymptotic speed-up proportional to the duplication factor across atoms. Empirically, the cache hit rate exceeds 50% on the proton+neutron+deuteron sweep.

Categorical interpretation

The recursive reducer forms the algorithmic content of the Markov-trace existence theorem for the Iwahori-Hecke algebra. The axioms uniquely determine the trace. The algorithm constructs the unique value for any input word. This contrasts with seminormal/Hoefsmit ascent, which realises the trace via the explicit Wedderburn decomposition H_n(q) \cong \bigoplus_\lambda M_{f^\lambda}. Both routes agree on values. The axiomatic route avoids reliance on Hoefsmit matrix elements.
